concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper-bound notation for growth rates of running time.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Formal sums of powers of an indeterminate with coefficients in a ring or field.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with real a, b and i squared equal to -1.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, where each step moves each head by at most one cell.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen n log n conjecture
concepts.gloss: The conjecture that n log n is the optimal order of growth for multiplying n-bit integers on a multitape Turing machine.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: A linear map that evaluates a sequence at powers of a root of unity, computing convolutions pointwise after transformation.

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: Multiplication of two coefficient sequences as polynomials modulo x^S - 1, so that exponents wrap around modulo S.

evidence.quote: convolution modulo xS − 1 has no nonzero wraparound

concepts.name: Radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Reduction of integer multiplication to a convolution of coefficient lists obtained by splitting each input into radix digits and propagating carries.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: A relabelling of a cyclic convolution of length S as a multidimensional cyclic convolution over pairwise coprime lengths, via the Chinese remainder theorem.

evidence.quote: Agarwal and Cooley used the Chinese remainder theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic convolution

concepts.name: Recursive rank saving
concepts.gloss: The recursion in which a call at parameter m uses s smaller calls with s < W m, so the cost per unit of volume is multiplied by a factor below m at each level and gives a power saving.

evidence.quote: that the total number s of smaller calls satisfies s < W m

concepts.name: Established O(n log n) multiplier

concepts.name: Signed coefficient packing

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Precision and exact recovery
